summary: NE PACK IN PITTSBURGH: all eight 14U teams in the Northeast Pack are ranked in the top 16 in the country, and they play 12 league games Friday through Sunday at three rinks north and west of Pittsburgh. Every team plays three times.

The chase: Mid-Fairfield (#1, 99.99) is 7-0 in the league with 21 points, has outscored opponents 46-13, and has not lost a game all season (29-0-3). Woodbridge Wolfpack (#6, 96.97) is second with 13 points, then Bishop Kearney Selects (#11, 96.24) and Mount St Charles (#7, 96.52) with 11 each, Chicago Mission (#5, 97.06) with 10, Pittsburgh Penguins Elite (#13, 96.15) with 8, NJ Rockets (#14, 95.97) with 6 and Chicago Reapers (#16, 95.74) with 4. A regulation win is worth 3 points, so second through sixth can reshuffle completely in one weekend.

Game of the weekend: Mid-Fairfield at Woodbridge Wolfpack, Saturday 4:00 PM. The Wolfpack came closest to Mid-Fairfield in league play, scoring five in a 7-5 loss on Oct 18. No one else in the league has put more than three past them.
Mid-Fairfield's other two: at Pittsburgh Penguins Elite on Friday (Mid-Fairfield won the first meeting 5-0) and home to Chicago Reapers on Sunday (5-1 the first time).

Mission's weekend: Chicago Mission visits Bishop Kearney on Friday (Mission won 7-4 on Oct 4), hosts Pittsburgh Penguins Elite on Saturday morning (Pens Elite won 4-3 in overtime on Oct 17) and finishes at NJ Rockets on Sunday (Mission won 5-1). Three regulation wins would put Mission at 19 points.

Swing games for the middle of the table: Wolfpack at Mount St Charles on Friday (Wolfpack won 4-3 on Oct 4), Bishop Kearney at Mount St Charles on Sunday (Bishop Kearney won 4-1), and Bishop Kearney at NJ Rockets on Saturday (the Rockets won 6-2). Wolfpack at Pens Elite on Sunday is a rematch of a game Pens Elite won.

Reapers need points: Chicago Reapers is 1-5 with an overtime loss and has dropped four straight in the league, including a 5-4 overtime loss to Mission. It opens against NJ Rockets on Friday at 8:00 AM, the team it beat 5-3 for its only league win.

Players to watch: Jack Brayman (Mid-Fairfield) leads the league with 8 goals and 17 points in 7 games. Michael Mufarreh (Chicago Mission) is the top-scoring defenseman with 4 goals and 12 points, tied for second overall with Jayden Widen (Mount St Charles, 6 goals). Mid-Fairfield has six of the league's top 15 scorers. In goal, Luke Thompson (Mid-Fairfield) is 5-0 and has allowed 8 goals in 5 games; Logan Morgida (Wolfpack) is 4-0.

Nashville in British Columbia: Nashville Jr. Predators (#9, 96.38) is the only American team in a six-team U15 prep event in Delta and Burnaby, Thursday through Sunday. It plays Delta Hockey Academy on Thursday at 12:30 PM, then Burnaby Winter Club Academy at 10:00 AM and St George's School at 8:00 PM on Friday. Yale Hockey Academy and Pacific Coast Academy are the other two teams. Placement games are Saturday, first against fourth and second against third, and the final is Sunday at 1:00 PM. Times are Pacific.

Elsewhere: Team Illinois (#4, 97.12) plays a four-game tournament in the Chicago suburbs against Madison Capitols, Midwest Warriors, Milwaukee Jr Admirals and CarShield. Biggby Coffee is at the Tier 1 Hockey Federation showcase near Pittsburgh with four games. Top Gun (Elite) meets Boston Jr Eagles (Elite) on Saturday morning in Salem, NH, and HB Detroit plays Victory Honda in a league game on Saturday.

summary: NE PACK IN PITTSBURGH: the top three 15U teams in the country are in the same building this weekend. Pittsburgh Penguins Elite (#1, 96.16), Bishop Kearney Selects (#2, 94.98) and Mount St Charles (#3, 94.97) are also first, second and third in some order in the Northeast Pack, and six of the league's eight teams are ranked in the top nine.

The standings: Bishop Kearney leads with 16 points (5-0 plus a shootout loss), Mount St Charles has 14 (5-1, five straight wins, a league-best 13 goals against), Pens Elite 13 and Chicago Reapers (#5, 93.66) 11. Woodbridge Wolfpack (#9, 92.78) has 8 and Chicago Mission (#8, 93.34) has 7.

Game of the weekend: Bishop Kearney at Pittsburgh Penguins Elite, Saturday 3:40 PM. #2 at #1, and Bishop Kearney won the first meeting 5-3 on Oct 3. Pens Elite's only two league losses are that game and a 4-3 shootout loss to Mount St Charles.

Bishop Kearney's test: the league leader opens against Wolfpack on Friday (a 3-2 win the first time), plays Pens Elite on Saturday, then visits Chicago Reapers on Sunday at 8:00 AM. The Reapers handed Bishop Kearney its only league loss, 7-6 in a shootout on Oct 17.

Mount St Charles can take over first: it plays Chicago Mission on Friday (won 5-2 on Oct 17), New Jersey Rockets on Saturday (won 8-1) and Wolfpack on Sunday (won 3-1). Its only loss was 5-2 to Bishop Kearney on opening weekend.

Reapers and Mission: Chicago Reapers has gone to a shootout three times, winning two, and sits fourth. Chicago Mission has dropped two straight, 5-2 to Mount St Charles and 2-1 in a shootout to the Reapers, and gets Mount St Charles and Pens Elite this weekend. Pens Elite won their first meeting.
Bottom of the table: Mid-Fairfield is 0-6 and has been outscored 40-10; New Jersey Rockets' only win was 5-4 over Mid-Fairfield. They meet again Sunday at 1:40 PM in the last 15U game of the weekend.

Players to watch: Arjun Mangadu (Mount St Charles) leads the league with 8 goals and 14 points in 6 games. Cameron Cline (Pens Elite) has 12 points, and Pens Elite defenseman Cameron Pelle has 9. In goal, Evan Ladd (Mount St Charles) is 4-0 with 6 goals against, and Nicholas Ryan (Pens Elite) is 3-0 with 7 against in 4 games.

Elsewhere: Oakland Jr Grizzlies (#6) plays Fox Motors twice in league play, Pittsburgh Vengeance and Palmyra Black Knights meet three times at Alpha Ice Complex, Victory Honda plays Indiana Elite twice on Saturday in Fort Wayne, and HB Detroit faces BioSteel Sports Academy on Saturday.

summary: QUIET WEEKEND AT THE TOP: none of the top 20 teams at 13U has a game this weekend. It is a lighter weekend for many of the top teams: several have nothing on the schedule ahead of Thanksgiving weekend, when the International Silver Stick in Whitby and other big tournaments begin.

Best series: Ohio Blue Jackets and Philadelphia Jr Flyers, both ranked in the low 20s and about a quarter of a rating point apart, play three times in Columbus: Friday 6:50 PM and Saturday 4:00 PM at Chiller Ice Works, then Sunday 11:10 AM at the OhioHealth Ice Haus. The Jr Flyers come in 18-5-1, the Blue Jackets 13-12-2.
Michigan league games on Sunday: Little Caesars (#4, 93.76) hosts Compuware at USA Hockey Arena at 11:40 AM, and HB Detroit plays Belle Tire at 10:00 AM in Lincoln Park.
Also: Windy City Storm hosts Indiana Elite on Sunday at noon at Orbit Ice Arena, and St Louis Blues plays Madison Capitols twice at Centene Community Ice Center.

ST. LOUIS TOURNAMENT: eight teams are at Centene Community Ice Center in Maryland Heights, Missouri, including six ranked in the top 20: Florida Alliance (#4), St Louis Blues (#10), Victory Honda (#15), Chicago Reapers (#16), Vegas Jr Golden Knights (#17) and Dallas Stars Elite (#20), plus Chicago Mission and Philadelphia Hockey Club.

One group has St Louis Blues, Chicago Mission, Dallas Stars Elite and Victory Honda playing each other Friday and Saturday morning. The other has Vegas, Chicago Reapers, Philadelphia Hockey Club and Florida Alliance. Later rounds follow on Saturday afternoon and Sunday.

Games to circle: Chicago Reapers vs Vegas Jr Golden Knights, Friday 9:00 AM, a meeting of #16 and #17. St Louis Blues vs Dallas Stars Elite, Friday 4:20 PM. Florida Alliance, the highest-ranked team in the field, plays Vegas on Saturday at 8:20 AM.
Chicago Mission has two games Friday: St Louis Blues at 9:10 AM and Victory Honda at 3:50 PM.

Elsewhere: Woodbridge Wolfpack hosts Red Bank Generals on Saturday, Long Island Royals plays New York City Hockey Club and New Jersey Colonials, and Cleveland Barons meets LA Jr Kings on Sunday in Michigan. The top three teams, Middlesex Islanders East, Little Caesars and Boston Advantage, are off.

summary: NEW ENGLAND ROAD TRIP: Mid-Fairfield (#4) has the busiest weekend of any top team, four league games in two days. It visits Providence Capitals (#13) twice on Saturday at Rhode Island Sports Center (9:00 AM and 1:15 PM), then Bay State Breakers (#16) twice on Sunday at the Bog Ice Arena (10:30 AM and 2:30 PM).
Close matchup: South Shore Kings (#9) plays Top Gun (#11) on Sunday at 9:25 AM at the ICENTER in Salem, NH.

Chicago: Windy City Storm gets two ranked visitors. Chicago Mission (#8) plays at Orbit Ice Arena on Saturday at 2:40 PM, and Chicago Fury (#15) plays the Storm on Sunday at 11:20 AM at Arctic Ice Arena.

Also: Providence Capitals finishes its weekend against Boston Jr Terriers on Sunday, Oakland Jr Grizzlies hosts HB Detroit, Philadelphia Little Flyers plays North Jersey Avalanche twice on Saturday, and Dallas Stars Elite (#7) plays Houston twice.

Not on the schedule this weekend: Little Caesars (#1), Pittsburgh Penguins Elite (#2) and Worcester Shamrocks (#3). It is a lighter weekend for many of the top teams: several have nothing on the schedule ahead of Thanksgiving weekend, when the International Silver Stick in Whitby and other big tournaments begin.

FRIDAY NIGHT IN ELK GROVE: St Louis Blues (#6, 96.8) visits Chicago Mission (#19, 94.6) on Friday at 7:40 PM at Elk Grove Ice Arena. It is the only game of the weekend between two top-25 Squirt teams.
Middlesex Islanders East (#7) plays Boston Jr Terriers on Sunday at 9:20 AM in Canton, MA.

New Jersey Rockets (#24) has three games: Long Island Royals on Saturday morning in Bridgewater, then Palmyra Black Knights twice on Sunday. Washington Little Capitals (#25) hosts New Jersey Colonials three times, and Long Island Gulls (#21) plays Long Island Royals on Sunday.
Off this weekend: Little Caesars (#1), Mid-Fairfield (#2), Buffalo Jr Sabres (#3), Team Illinois (#4) and Top Gun (#5).
